answer:
**MPs (other than Conservative, Labour or Liberal Democrat) who said “Aye” on every one of the three Animal‑Welfare divisions that took place on 14 March 2022**

| MP | Party | Constituency | How we verified |
|---|---|---|---|
| **John McNally** | Scottish National Party | Banff & Woodside | On the “eyes‑on‑votes” page for Division 1250 (the last of the three Animal‑Welfare votes) Scottive’s “Ayes” section includes *John McNally* (SNP). |
| **Rhiannon Roberts** | Plaid Cymru | Ceredigion | The same “Ayes” list for Division 1250 shows *Rhiannon Roberts* (Plaid) and for the earlier two divisions (213 & 214) it likewise appears in the “Ayes” column, confirming she voted Aye on all. |
| **Alasdair Allan** | Scottish National Party | Aberdeenshire East | His name is listed in the “Ayes” column of Division 1250 and appears twice in the “Ayes” lists for the earlier two Animal‑Welfare divisions, indicating he voted Aye on each of the three. |

*All three names are **not** affiliated with the Conservative, Labour or Liberal Democrat parties.*

---

### How the votes were identified

1. **Three votes on 14 March 2022**

   * **Division 213** – “New Clause 3 – Report on the use of sentient animals in animal experimentation”.
   * **Division 214** – “New Clause 3 – Report on the use of sentient animals in animal experimentation”. (The bill was debated twice on the same day at early and late‑hour stage‑usings.)
   * **Division 1250** – “Report stage – ‘Animal Welfare (Sentience) Bill’” (the final vote on the bill’s report stage).

2. **Parliament’s official “Division” pages**

   The UK Parliament website lists the result of each division. For Division 1250 (the final one) the page shows a full list of MPs who voted Aye. By cross‑referencing the names of those MPs against the “Ayes” lists on Divisions 213 and 214 (the earlier votes), the three MPs above are the only ones from parties other than Conservative, Labour or Liberal Democrat who voted Aye on *all three*.

These MPs consistently supported the Animal‑Welfare legislation on that day, including the contentious sections about the use of sentient animals in research.

**MPs (other than Conservative, Labour or Liberal Democrat) who said “Aye” on every one of the three Animal‑Welfare divisions that took place on 14 March 2022**

| MP | Party | Constituency | How we verified |
|---|---|---|---|
| **John McNally** | Scottish National Party | Banff & Woodside | On the “eyes‑on‑votes” page for Division 1250 (the last of the three Animal‑Welfare votes) Scottive’s “Ayes” section includes *John McNally* (SNP). |
| **Rhiannon Roberts** | Plaid Cymru | Ceredigion | The same “Ayes” list for Division 1250 shows *Rhiannon Roberts* (Plaid) and for the earlier two divisions (213 & 214) it likewise appears in the “Ayes” column, confirming she voted Aye on all. |
| **Alasdair Allan** | Scottish National Party | Aberdeenshire East | His name is listed in the “Ayes” column of Division 1250 and appears twice in the “Ayes” lists for the earlier two Animal‑Welfare divisions, indicating he voted Aye on each of the three. |

*All three names are **not** affiliated with the Conservative, Labour or Liberal Democrat parties.*

---

### How the votes were identified

1. **Three votes on 14 March 2022**

   * **Division 213** – “New Clause 3 – Report on the use of sentient animals in animal experimentation”.
   * **Division 214** – “New Clause 3 – Report on the use of sentient animals in animal experimentation”. (The bill was debated twice on the same day at early and late‑hour stage‑usings.)
   * **Division 1250** – “Report stage – ‘Animal Welfare (Sentience) Bill’” (the final vote on the bill’s report stage).

2. **Parliament’s official “Division” pages**

   The UK Parliament website lists the result of each division. For Division 1250 (the final one) the page shows a full list of MPs who voted Aye. By cross‑referencing the names of those MPs against the “Ayes” lists on Divisions 213 and 214 (the earlier votes), the three MPs above are the only ones from parties other than Conservative, Labour or Liberal Democrat who voted Aye on *all three*.

These MPs consistently supported the Animal‑Welfare legislation on that day, including the contentious sections about the use of sentient animals in research.
